<reason>A better justified the supplementary tax and answered the central implementation objections. B’s repeal examples established meaningful practical risk, but its claim that A’s inability to identify one missing historical feature proved the proposal indistinguishable from failed systems overstated the concession. B also repeatedly blurred asset transfers with escaping worldwide liability and treated restricted deferral as the entire policy. A’s distinctions between liquid and illiquid fortunes, and annual obligations versus taxation at death, supplied the cleaner comparative case.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A answered the estate-tax analogy by distinguishing wealth held each year from wealth remaining at death, while emphasizing that liquid fortunes pay currently. This directly undermined B’s claim that annual valuation merely adds redundant machinery to delayed collection.</best_rebuttal>
